meanings.en: to choose, select; to use up completely (quotas, limits)
meanings.note: + acc. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'брать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to choose, use up', paired with 'выбирать'.

examples.trans: This year all the quotas have been used up.

Agreed, I will choose a movie.

meanings.note: Exclamation of surprise or dismay. Core Russian interj meaning 'Good Lord!' in everyday speech.

В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Дай! = give (me)!. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'есть'). Used in Russian as a perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to finish eating', forming an aspectual pair with 'доедать'.

examples.text: Он доел весь суп до конца.
examples.trans: He finished eating all the soup to the end.

examples.text: А проигравший повар обязан доесть всё сам.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.
